ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a billboard AB on top of the building. From point D, which is 12 meters away from the building BC, the angle of elevation to the top A of the billboard is $37^\circ$, and the angle of elevation to the bottom B of the billboard is $30^\circ$. Calculate the height of the billboard AB. (Leave the result in square root form, reference data: $\sin 37^\circ \approx 0.60$, $\cos 37^\circ \approx 0.80$, $\tan 37^\circ \approx 0.75$)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the problem, we know\\
$\angle ADC=37^\circ$, $\angle BDC=30^\circ$, $CD=12$ meters, $AC\perp DC$.\\
In $\triangle DCA$, $\tan\angle ADC=\frac{AC}{CD}$, thus\\
$AC=CD\cdot \tan\angle ADC=12\times \tan37^\circ\approx 12\times 0.75=9$ meters.\\
In $\triangle DBC$, $\tan\angle BDC=\frac{BC}{CD}$, thus\\
$BC=CD\cdot \tan\angle BDC=12\times \tan30^\circ=12\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=4\sqrt{3}$ meters.\\
Therefore, $AB=AC−BC=9−4\sqrt{3}$.\\
Answer: The height of the billboard $AB$ is $\boxed{9−4\sqrt{3}}$ meters.
